whatis.h2: What is an early payment discount?
whatis.intro: An early payment discount is a price cut your supplier offers if you pay an invoice before the due date. It is written as terms such as 2/10 net 30: 2% off within 10 days, or the full amount by day 30. In effect, the supplier pays you to settle 20 days sooner.

cards.title: An offer, not a term you owe
cards.body: Skip it and you simply pay $22.56 a case by day 30. Take it and the same case is $22.11, paid by day 10.
cards.alt: Open book, for taking or skipping the early pay offer

cards.title: A deadline with no grace
cards.body: Day 11 is too late. Taking the 2% after the window is called an unearned discount, and suppliers often bill it back.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for the hard deadline on the discount window

cards.title: Offering it costs the same rate
cards.body: If you offer 2/10 net 30 to your own accounts, the math runs the other way. An account that would otherwise pay on day 30 costs you 37.2% a year to pay 20 days sooner.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for offering early pay terms to your own accounts

who.h2: Who uses an early payment discount calculator
who.intro: Each invoice on early pay terms asks a distributor's payables team the same thing: pay early for the discount, or keep the cash? The person who approves supplier invoices, plans the payment run or negotiates terms should run it first.

look.h2: Read the terms before you take the discount
look.intro: The yearly rate is plain arithmetic. The risk sits in the terms you enter and the invoice behind them, so test both against a real invoice.

steps.title: When the 10 days start
steps.body: Most terms count the 10 days from the invoice date, not the day the product arrives. Slow approvals eat into that window before any payment can go out.

steps.title: How your volume tier is paid
steps.body: The calculator takes the 6% off the invoice before the 2%. If your tier comes back later as a rebate, the invoice stays at $24.00, so enter the volume discount as 0%.

steps.title: Whether the invoice is right
steps.body: The calculator trusts the $24.00 you type. Ten days is not long to check a delivery against its invoice, and paying early on a wrong one leaves you chasing a credit.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits when you are the buyer
vos.h3: Supplier payments stay with you and your books
vos.body: VOS does not calculate discounts, pay suppliers or touch your payables. Its part is the sale, not the purchase: each order your accounts place by voice in the VOS app comes in confirmed and timestamped. Paying early stays your decision, made in your own books.

next.intro: The discount decides when you pay suppliers. These three cover when your accounts pay you, what you paid against standard, and what a deal really saved.
